text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-President Hrawi said the latest Israeli air raids on south Lebanon showed that Israel was not ready to negotiate peace.
-Papal nuncio Puente said Pope John Paul would probably visit Lebanon for up to 48 hours in May.
-Middle East Airlines will complete a $125 million capital increase on Saturday.
-Pro-Iranian Hizbollah chief sheikh Nasrallah said: "Israel must cease to exist, and it will".
-An investigating magistrate demanded up to ten years imprisonment for three Lebanese charged with importing plastic toxic waste from Germany in 1996.
-Israeli helicopters attacked an abandoned house in south Lebanon.
-Middle East Airlines made a $50 million loss in 1996.
-French Defence Minister Millon said President Chirac would mediate between Israel and both Syria and Lebanon.
-The Bank of Lebanon issued certificates of deposit dated February 14 to commercial banks worth 69 billion Lebanese pounds.
